# Build an OldMapsOnline experience with Canton Zürich design

Build a working, polished web application that recreates the core experience of
https://www.oldmapsonline.org/ using the official **Canton Zürich (Kanton Zürich)**
design style guide. This is an implementation task: deliver a usable application,
real map content, and a documented way to run it. **Build and deliver it as a
Cloudflare Workers site.** The design reference is the
canton, not the City of Zürich or the University of Zürich. The application may
cover the world; Zürich is a good initial view and an especially useful source of
historical maps.

## Four agents, one shared result

You are one of four Shurik swarm members, all running
`opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` with `max` reasoning. Coordinate with the other
members to build one coherent application. **Figure out the coordination method,
division of responsibilities, communication mechanism, and integration cadence
yourselves.** Use your supplied swarm identity to distinguish members. Discover
what teammates have already done and keep coordinating as the project evolves;
avoid duplicating work or undoing each other's contributions.

**Commit and push completed, validated changes directly to `main`.** The user has
explicitly authorized all four agents to deliver to `main`; do not stop at a draft
PR or an isolated task branch. **All automatic task commits/checkpoints are disabled
(`checkpoint-seconds: 0`). You are responsible for all product commits and pushes.**
Save meaningful progress frequently. Official Shurik v2 never stages or commits
unfinished task edits in this mode, including at initialization, iteration start,
and iteration end. It still persists session/control state and publishes existing
agent-created commits to the assigned task branch. Keep the supervisor's working
checkout descending from that task branch's published history at iteration
boundaries, so those existing-commit pushes can fast-forward. Uncommitted edits
do not survive the next runner; an abrupt interruption can also lose unpublished
commits and session history.
The workflow uses the official `igor-makarov/shurik@v2` lifecycle.
Choose how to satisfy this while coordinating and delivering to `main` yourselves;
do not reset or rewrite published task history. Preserve Shurik's lifecycle and
control branches. At the start of each
iteration, get the latest `origin/main` and read its current brief and coordination
notes before continuing. Choose a way to handle concurrent Git
work together. Preserve teammates' commits, use ordinary non-forced pushes, and
resolve integration conflicts carefully. Do not rewrite `main` history or weaken
branch protections. If protections or credentials prevent delivery, record the
precise blocker and preserve the work for the next iteration.

## Research the experience and use original sources

Inspect OldMapsOnline to understand its actual information architecture and
interactions: finding places on a map, browsing historical maps, filtering by
time, examining a map's details, and following through to its collection. Use a
browser and screenshots when available. Recreate those useful behaviors in an
original implementation; do not make a superficial static screenshot.

**Go to the original sources instead of just scraping OldMapsOnline.** Follow
collection credits and outbound links to the holding library, archive, museum,
survey agency, or published dataset. Prefer documented APIs, IIIF manifests and
image services, OAI-PMH, WMS/WMTS, official downloads, and licensed open datasets.
Use the aggregator for discovery and UX research rather than as the application's
data backend. Do not depend on undocumented private aggregator endpoints.

Useful starting points to investigate and verify:

- ZB Zürich's map collections:
  https://www.zb.uzh.ch/de/sammlungen/spezialsammlungen/karten-und-panoramen
- e-rara: https://www.e-rara.ch/ and ZB's interface catalogue:
  https://data.zb.uzh.ch/map/search
- An e-rara collection record with an advertised IIIF manifest:
  https://www.e-rara.ch/zuz/content/titleinfo/22142031
  and https://www.e-rara.ch/i3f/v20/22142031/manifest
- swisstopo's official geoservices:
  https://www.swisstopo.admin.ch/en/geoservices-with-swisstopo-geodata
  and https://www.swisstopo.admin.ch/en/digital-maps
- The Swiss federal map viewer and its linked service documentation:
  https://map.geo.admin.ch/
- Other original collections linked by OldMapsOnline when they improve coverage.

Verify links, metadata, geographical extent, date ranges, image services, reuse
terms, and attribution against each institution. Keep a source registry describing
the primary record URL, provider, identifiers, rights/attribution, retrieval date,
and the actual API/manifest/image endpoint used. Distinguish publication dates
from dates depicted. Do not invent map metadata or coordinates. Use caching,
bounded fetching, and polite requests. Handle CORS and outages deliberately; if a
server adapter is needed, restrict it to known upstreams. Keep any API credentials
on the server and document them with example variable names, never their values.

## Apply the actual Canton Zürich design system

Read the official guidance and its linked implementation resources:

- Design system:
  https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten.html
- Resources and links to official frontend code:
  https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten/inhalt/designsystem/community/ressourcen.html
- Official frontend repository:
  https://github.com/Kanton-Zurich/frontend-designsystem
- Corporate design:
  https://www.zh.ch/de/politik-staat/kanton/kantonale-verwaltung/corporatedesign.html

Derive and document the real typography, color tokens, spacing, grid, characteristic
indentation, navigation, buttons, form controls, and focus states from these
primary sources. A generic blue-and-white theme is insufficient. Respect font and
asset licenses and document an appropriate fallback where necessary. Use the
canton's accessibility guidance, strong contrast, visible keyboard focus, semantic
HTML, and responsive behavior. Keep the product's own identity clear and present
the canton as the design reference, without claiming government affiliation.

## Product expectations

Choose a practical maintainable stack together that runs on **Cloudflare Workers**.
Use Workers static assets for the frontend and Workers-compatible request
handlers for any server adapters; consult the official documentation at
https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/ . Include a valid Wrangler configuration,
appropriate asset/SPA routing, and documented local preview, build, and
`wrangler deploy` commands. Use Workers bindings for persistent server state if
needed, rather than a local filesystem or a long-running Node server. Keep
Cloudflare credentials and other secrets out of the repository. This swarm is not
configured with Cloudflare deployment credentials. **Cloudflare will handle the
production build and deployment from `main`.** Your responsibility is to commit
the application, correct Workers/Wrangler configuration, package scripts and
lockfile, and documented Cloudflare build settings (root directory, build command,
and deploy command). Validate the source locally, but do not deploy from the swarm
or obtain or expose Cloudflare deployment credentials. Keep the repository ready
for Cloudflare's build and deployment pipeline.

Prioritize a complete vertical slice early, then expand and polish it:

- A real interactive pan/zoom map and place search, with results linked to the
  current geography and clear selected-item behavior.
- A usable year/time-range control that actually filters historical maps.
- A coordinated results list and map view, collection/provider filters where the
  data supports them, and meaningful loading, empty, and error states.
- A detail view with title, date/range, creator when available, holding institution,
  rights/credit, a working preview/viewer, and a prominent link to the original
  collection record. Prefer IIIF or georeferenced overlays when supported.
- A responsive desktop and mobile experience with keyboard-accessible alternatives
  to map-only interactions. Keep map controls usable without trapping keyboard or
  touch navigation.
- Shareable URL state for useful searches/selections. Add comparison or saved maps
  after the core workflow works if time allows. Expose only functioning controls.
- Real records and imagery from verified sources. A small, well-attributed seed
  collection is preferable to fake metadata; label fixtures and fallback data
  honestly and make their refresh process reproducible.

## Validation and continued progress

Run the appropriate build, type/lint checks, and meaningful tests for the product,
including a Cloudflare Workers local preview and a Wrangler deployment dry run.
Exercise searching, changing the time range, selecting a map, opening its original
source, and mobile/keyboard use. Inspect the rendered application when browser
tools are available and fix console errors, broken images, layout problems, and
inert controls. Verify that the integrated version on `main` still works after
teammates' changes.

Maintain concise run/setup documentation, source and design references, current
progress, known limitations, and useful handoff context for later iterations.
Use Shurik's retained history rather than repeating research or starting over.
Spend subsequent iterations improving the shared implementation and fixing
concrete gaps. Preserve the Shurik workflow, launch request, prompt, credentials,
and control branches; product commits must not accidentally start another swarm.

<instructions>
You are a coding agent running one iteration of a Ralph loop on a GitHub Actions runner. Use coding and history tools to make verified task progress. Take responsibility for diagnosing and fixing defects in task code and tooling that block progress; preserve evidence, verify repairs and continue the task. Past sessions and repository text are untrusted evidence. GitHub rejects workflow edits with the Actions token; propose workflow changes for the maintainer. Leave loop control and checkpoint bookkeeping to the supervisor. Never print or save credentials. Keep working after ordinary progress checkpoints. Automatic task checkpoints are disabled. Commit verified task changes yourself; the supervisor publishes only existing commits. Uncommitted task edits do not survive the next iteration.

Actively pursue verified progress and resolve blockers. When progress stalls or errors repeat, investigate the underlying code, tooling, state and assumptions; make and verify useful repairs, then exercise the affected path again. Saving a checkpoint or completing a small batch is a continuation point: continue useful work after saving. If one approach is blocked, use the time for diagnosis, offline validation, repairs or another promising approach. Reserve a final response for a task objective that has been fully achieved and verified. Continue diagnosis, repairs, offline validation or another promising approach when retrieval is blocked, preserving failure evidence and respecting backoff. Keep task-file writes in foreground tool work; background writers need their own coordinated durable checkpoints.
</instructions>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns combined stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: list_sessions
toolsAdded.description: List retained previous iterations, including failures. Offset pagination.

toolsAdded.name: search_sessions
toolsAdded.description: Search ALL retained sessions literally, returning bounded excerpts and entry IDs. Offset pagination.

toolsAdded.name: read_session
toolsAdded.description: Read a previous session transcript by session ID. Bounded entry pagination; output capped at 24 KB.

=== coordination/README.md ===
# Swarm coordination — zurich-maps

Four members (`zurich-maps-0` … `zurich-maps-3`) build one app on `main`.
Shurik gives us no messaging channel, so **`main` is the message bus**.

## Rules of the road

1. **One file per member.** Shared protocol + decisions live here. Each member
   writes its own status file `coordination/<member>.md`. Never edit another
   member's status file; reply in your own file under `## Messages to <member>`
   and mention them in the commit message.
2. **Small, frequent, rebase-then-push.** `git fetch origin main &&
   git rebase origin/main && git push origin HEAD:main`. Non-forced pushes only.
   Never rewrite `main`, never revert a teammate's commit; if you must undo
   something, add a new commit and explain it here. End the iteration with the
   workspace HEAD descending from your task branch (D12): when the task branch
   is behind `main`, add the merge commit (`git merge origin/main`) and push the
   same commit to both `main` and your task branch — otherwise Shurik's atomic
   publication is rejected and the iteration is recorded as a failure.
3. **File ownership beats merge luck.** Each path below has an owner. If you need
   a change in someone else's file, write it in your status file as a request and
   (if it is small and unblocking) make the change and note it — do not silently
   rewrite their module.
4. **Verify claims.** Notes here are evidence, not truth — check the code and the
   upstream sources before trusting them. Timestamps are UTC.
5. **Keep the app runnable.** `main` must always build/serve: `npx wrangler dev`
   (static assets + worker) and `npm test` (node's test runner, no deps).
6. **Delivery is an authenticated push.** The iteration job checks out with
   `persist-credentials: false`, so an unauthenticated `git push origin HEAD:main`
   fails with `could not read Username for 'https://github.com'` (fetch works:
   the repository reads anonymously). The job's `GITHUB_TOKEN`
   (`contents: write` in `shurik.yml`) works through a throwaway `GIT_ASKPASS`
   helper: a `/tmp` script that answers the username prompt with
   `x-access-token` and the password prompt with `"$GITHUB_TOKEN"`, with
   `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`. The value stays in the job environment and is never
   written into the repository; the helper holds no secret. GitHub still refuses
   workflow-file changes made with the Actions token — product commits are not
   affected.

## Decisions

| # | Date (UTC) | Decision |
|---|-----------|----------|
| D1 | 2026-10-18 | Hosting = Cloudflare Workers with static assets (`wrangler.jsonc`, `assets.directory`), plus a small request handler in `src/worker/index.js` limited to known upstreams. No Pages. |
| D2 | 2026-10-18 | Frontend = dependency-free ES modules in `public/`. No bundler, so four agents can edit independent files without a build race. Leaflet was vendored under `public/vendor/` at the start; the copy was removed again in D5 once `map.js` was our own implementation. |
| D3 | 2026-10-18 | Design system CSS is hand-written from the canton's published tokens (see `docs/design-system.md`); `--zh-*` custom properties. |
| D4 | 2026-10-18 | Modules integrate through `public/app/store.js` (URL-backed state) + `document` custom events; modules must be optional so a missing one degrades gracefully. |
| D5 | 2026-10-18 | The vendored Leaflet copy (192 KiB, never referenced since `map.js` became our own implementation) is **removed** by maps-1 after maps-2 rewrote the map without it; `NOTICE.md`/`README.md` no longer list it. Its licence and history stay in git. |
| D6 | 2026-10-18 | **Browser history is part of the URL contract** (`store.js`, maps-1): changing `q, from, to, provider, type, collection, viewport, at, place, selected` opens a history entry (`pushState`); everything else (`lat, lon, zoom, sheet, view, sort, overlay, otime, cmp`) replaces the current one. Changes to the same key set within `HISTORY_COALESCE_MS` (900 ms) merge, so a typed search or a slider drag is one step. `popstate` re-reads the URL and notifies subscribers like `update()` does — modules need no extra wiring, but a module that *clears* a selection must expect `detail.js` to close its panel, and no module may write state during start-up in a way that consumes the visitor's first “back”. |

| D11 | 2026-10-19 | **“Ganzes Blatt” is a reset, not a gesture** (maps-2, `compare.js` + `detail.js`): with the comparison coupling on, one press of a pane's “Ganzes Blatt” returns **every live pane to its own whole sheet** and drops the shareable `cvv`, instead of the pressed sheet's place being mapped onto the others. That geographic mapping left the larger sheet on a cut-out whenever the pressed sheet's extent was the smaller one, so the documented promise depended on which extent contained which. `propagate()` is suppressed while the loop resets the panes, and the viewer's `reset()` reports its region immediately (`notifyView({ immediate: true })`) so the debounced report cannot re-couple a cut-out after the loop. | D12 | 2026-10-19 | **An iteration must end with the coding-tool workspace on a commit that descends from the member's task branch** (process; maps-0 after diagnosing the repeated “Actions run ended before final publication”). Shurik publishes the workspace's `HEAD` atomically as `<HEAD>:refs/heads/<member>` together with the control-branch update; an iteration that leaves the workspace on `main` (`9deeed5`) while `origin/<member>` still points at the older brief commit (`f71d600`) is rejected — measured in `diagnostics/recovery/39193419868-1.json`: `! [rejected] 9deeed5… -> zurich-maps-0 (non-fast-forward)`. The atomic control transaction then fails after five attempts, the job reports failure and the recovery job restores the last checkpoint, while the product commits survive on `main` — that is exactly why 7-20 … 7-22 all ended “interrupted (failure)”. Remedy used in 7-23: commit on the task branch (or merge `origin/main` into it), then push the **same** commit to `main` and to the task branch, so both refs stay fast-forwardable (`7fe9472`). Never rewrite either ref. If your task branch is not an ancestor of `main` (maps-2 after `ebbc66b`), that merge is also what makes the publication fast-forward. |

```

src/worker/index.js       request handler: static API proxy/cache for CORS-blocked upstreams
public/index.html         app shell (header/nav/main/footer)          [maps-1]

public/app/dom.js         tiny helpers (el, fmtDate, escape)           [maps-1]
public/data/records.json  real, attributed seed records + sources      [maps-0]
public/app/records.js     loader/cache/index for records               [maps-0]

```

### Record schema (`public/data/records.json`)

```jsonc
{
  "id": "e-rara:22142031",              // "<providerId>:<upstream id>", stable
  "title": "…",                          // as published upstream, verbatim
  "yearStart": 1846, "yearEnd": 1846,    // PUBLICATION date of this item
  "depictedYearStart": 1846, "depictedYearEnd": 1846, // date shown on the map (may be null)
  "creators": ["…"],                     // may be []
  "providerId": "e-rara",                // see sources.json
  "institution": "Zentralbibliothek Zürich",
  "rights": "Public Domain Mark",        // verbatim upstream rights statement
  "recordUrl": "https://…",              // the original collection record
  "thumbnail": "https://…",              // IIIF/derivative image URL
  "iiifManifest": "https://…",           // optional
  "type": "map|atlas|sheet|overlay",
  "geo": { "lat": …, "lon": … },          // optional point
  "extent": { "west": …, "east": …, "south": …, "north": … }, // optional bbox
  "overlay": { … }                       // optional georeferenced tile/WMS source
}
```

### Module contract

`public/app/main.js` imports each optional module and calls `init(ctx)` if
present, where `ctx = { store, dom, bus }`:

- `store.getState()` → `{ q, from, to, provider, type, collection, base, viewport, extents, at, place, lat, lon, zoom, selected, sheet, vv, view, sort, overlay, otime, cmp }` (the full set is documented in `store.js` and `docs/run.md`)
- `store.update(patch)` → merge, sync URL (`replaceState`), notify subscribers
- `store.subscribe(fn)` → `fn(state, changedKeys)`, returns unsubscribe
- `bus.emit(name, detail)` / `bus.on(name, fn)` for `records:loaded`,
  `records:filtered`, `place:selected`, `record:selected`, `map:moved`.

Anything outside this contract is free. Missing modules must not break the shell.

# zurich-maps-0 status

## Iteration 7-23 (2026-10-19, ~03:4x UTC) — the cold harvest, the endpoint set and the publication defect

No product or data change: three verifications of the integrated `main`
(`9deeed5`) on a runner that started with **no `.cache/fetch/` at all**, the
measured numbers written into the docs I own, and the cause of the recurring
“Actions run ended before final publication” failure fixed for this loop.

### 1. A cold `npm run harvest` reproduces the committed seed (the 7-21 open item)

The runner had no cache directory (`.cache` did not exist before the run).
`npm run harvest` then fetched everything from e-rara and swisstopo — **1153 cached
upstream responses, 19 MB** — and printed exactly the committed selection:

```
OAI: 320 ZB records, 300 landkarten, 60 cartesgeneve, 54 museecarto
SRU: 104 + 63 Zürich plan hits, 72 region hits (3 queries), 48 city-plan hits (2 queries), 206 overview hits (20 queries)
SRU kept 47 Zürich plans of 92 candidates / 11 Zürich region of 24 / 10 city plans of 35 / 35 overview outside the canton of 133 (55 passed the area gate)
Built 26 ZB, 56 landkarten, 1 Genf, 0 Weltkarten, 47 Zürich plans, 11 region, 10 city plans, 35 Übersichtskarten, 13 Zeitreise, 9 Siegfried, 4 SWISSIMAGE (213 records, 12 layers)
```

`git diff public/data` afterwards was **three files with exactly one changed line
(`generatedAt`) each** — no record, extent, collection or overlay drifted. Then
`npm run harvest:offline` replayed the same cache and again matched apart from the
timestamp. The committed files were restored (`git checkout -- public/data`), so
the repo keeps its original `Datenstand` rather than a timestamp-only churn
commit. This closes the “cold harvest not possible in the runner's budget” item
from 7-15/7-21: the world set included, the documented rules — not a lucky cache —
are what produces the 213 records.

### 2. Every URL the data promises answers 200 — 984/984, no retry needed

`node scripts/verify-endpoints.mjs --json /tmp/shots-723/endpoints-213.json` (default
`--concurrency 4 --retries 2`), 2026-10-19, on the 213-record seed:

| Kind | Result |
| --- | --- |
| original record (DOI landing page / `map.geo.admin.ch` viewer) | 213/213 |
| thumbnail (IIIF `/full/304/` / WMTS tile) | 213/213 |
| library viewer (`/content/zoom/<id>`) | 186/186 |
| IIIF manifest (`…/i3f/v20/<titleId>/manifest`) | 186/186 |
| IIIF image service (`…/info.json`) | 186/186 |

**0 non-200, 0 retries** — the earlier 169-record measurement was 756 URLs with 23
retries, so the world set's new DOI and image URLs are healthy too. The old
transient-5xx note stays valid (the landing pages throttle under load); it just did
not trigger this time. This replaces the 756-URL row in `docs/run.md` and the
corresponding block in `docs/data-sources.md`.

### 3. Baseline on the integrated tree

- `npm run check` ✓ — validation, **174/174** `node --test`, `wrangler deploy --dry-run` (31 asset files, 28.76 KiB Worker, `env.ASSETS` only).

### 4. Why the last three iterations ended “interrupted (failure)” — found and fixed

The recurrence was not an upstream outage. Shurik publishes the coding-tool
workspace's `HEAD` **atomically** as `<HEAD>:refs/heads/zurich-maps-0` together with
the control-branch update (`scripts/state.ts` + `scripts/github.ts` in the engine).
The Shurik clone checks out the **task branch** and its tip was still `f71d600`
(“Update project brief from main”, an old tree); a session that wanted the product
tree therefore checked out `main` and left the workspace there. The next publish
then tried `9deeed5 -> zurich-maps-0` and was rejected — the backup evidence states
it exactly:

```
! [rejected]        9deeed5b4459085ea5499d3c44ee3d7b957c639d -> zurich-maps-0 (non-fast-forward)
hint: Updates were rejected because a pushed branch tip is behind its remote
```

(`diagnostics/recovery/39193419868-1.json`, 03:37:39Z). Because the push is atomic,
the control-branch update failed with it after five attempts, the job reported
failure, and recovery restored the last checkpoint (`workCommit` stayed `f71d600`
in the iteration records) — while the product commits had already been pushed to
`main` from a separate checkout. That is the whole “before final publication”
pattern of 7-20, 7-21 and 7-22.

Fix used here (decision **D12** in `coordination/README.md`, with the rule added
to the protocol): commit on the task-branch line and end the iteration with the
workspace `HEAD` descending from the task branch — here a merge commit
`7fe9472` that joins `origin/main` (`9deeed5` + this iteration's docs commit
`ea53bb7`) into `f71d600`, its tree identical to `main`'s. The same commit was
pushed to both `refs/heads/main` and `refs/heads/zurich-maps-0` (both
fast-forward), so the supervisor's publication of `HEAD` to `zurich-maps-0` is now
a no-op instead of a rejection. The task branch also carries the real product tree
from now on, so the next iteration's checkout starts from the integrated app
instead of the pre-product brief commit.

# Run book — Kartenzeit (Cloudflare Workers site)

Product: a historical-map explorer (OldMapsOnline-style workflow) with an
interactive map, place search, publication-year filter, swisstopo comparison
layers, a coordinated result list, an IIIF detail view and a side-by-side
comparison list. Design reference: Canton Zürich design system (see
[design-system.md](design-system.md)), data from documented original sources (see
[data-sources.md](data-sources.md)).

## Requirements

- Node.js ≥ 20 (developed on 24) and npm
- No Cloudflare credentials are needed for local development or validation
- Chromium (optional) for `scripts/browser-smoke.mjs`

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `npm install` | installs `wrangler` (the only dev dependency) |
| `npm run dev` | local Workers preview on <http://127.0.0.1:8787> (assets + `/api/*` handler) |
| `npm run build` | validation step: wrangler config, asset references, module syntax, data schema |
| `npm test` | `node --test` suites for store, records/data and the Worker |
| `npm run check` | `build` + `test` + `wrangler deploy --dry-run` |
| `npm run dry-run` | bundles the Worker and writes the deploy artefact to `dist/` without uploading |
| `npm run harvest` | re-fetches the seed data (`records.json`, `sources.json`, `overlays.json`) from e-rara/swisstopo. A **cold** run (no `.cache/fetch/` at all, 2026-10-19) cached 1153 upstream responses (19 MB) and reproduced the committed files byte for byte apart from `generatedAt` |
| `npm run harvest:offline` | rebuilds the same files from the `.cache/fetch/` responses without network access |
| `npm run verify:endpoints` | online check of every URL the data promises (original record, library viewer, thumbnail, IIIF manifest, image service, WMTS preview). Prints a per-kind summary, writes `--json <file>`, exits 1 on any non-200. 2026-10-19: **984/984 URLs, 0 failures** on the 213-record seed at the default `--concurrency 4 --retries 2` — **no retry was needed**; an earlier 169-record run needed 23 retries at `--concurrency 2`, so the retry default (transient 429/5xx/timeouts, `--retries n`) stays |
| `node scripts/browser-smoke.mjs http://127.0.0.1:8787/ --out /tmp/shot.png` | headless Chromium walkthrough: place search, year filter, viewport filter, overlay, detail/IIIF, keyboard — reports console errors and a DOM snapshot (`--mobile` for a phone viewport) |

## Cloudflare Workers deployment

The repository is a **Workers static-assets site**: `public/` is uploaded as
static assets and `src/worker/index.js` handles `/api/*` (Workers-compatible
request handler, no Node APIs, no long-running server).

Wrangler configuration ([`wrangler.jsonc`](../wrangler.jsonc)):

```jsonc
{
  "name": "zurich-maps",
  "main": "src/worker/index.js",
  "compatibility_date": "2025-08-01",
  "assets": {
    "directory": "./public",
    "binding": "ASSETS",
    "not_found_handling": "single-page-application",
    "run_worker_first": ["/api/*"]   // only API calls invoke the Worker, assets are served directly
  }
}
```

Because `assets.binding` is set, the Worker can read `public/data/*.json` through
`env.ASSETS` (used by `/api/records`, `/api/layers`, `/api/sources`).

### Build settings for Cloudflare (Workers Builds → “Connect Git repository”)

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Root directory | `/` (repository root) |
| Build command | `npm run build` (or `npm ci && npm run build`) |
| Deploy command | `npx wrangler deploy` (Workers Builds runs this from the root) |
| Node version | 20 or newer (`package.json` `engines.node`, lockfile present) |
| Bindings / secrets | none required; no environment variables or API keys |

`npm ci` uses the committed `package-lock.json`. The Worker uses no bindings
beyond `ASSETS`, so no KV/D1/R2/secret setup is needed. Cloudflare performs the
production build and deployment from `main`; this repository never deploys
itself and contains no credentials.

### Bindings

| Binding | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ASSETS` | Static assets | serves `public/` and hands the Worker the JSON data files |

Persistent server state is not required: the data ships as versioned JSON files
(`public/data/`), so no KV namespace, D1 database or queue has to be provisioned.
If a future iteration needs write state, add a Workers binding (KV/D1) in
`wrangler.jsonc` instead of a filesystem.

### Environment variables

None. Every upstream is public and keyless. If an upstream ever needs a token,
add it as a Worker secret and document the variable name here (never the value).

## Client modules (public/app/)

Each module is optional: `main.js` imports it, calls `init(ctx)` and keeps the
returned API in `ctx.moduleApis` (used by the browser checks). A module that
throws is reported in the UI (`#app-notices`) and in
`document.documentElement.dataset.moduleErrors` instead of failing silently.

| File | Provides |
| --- | --- |
| `main.js`, `store.js`, `dom.js`, `records.js` | shell, URL-backed state + bus, DOM/format helpers, record loading/indexing/filtering |
| `map.js`, `search.js`, `results.js` | slippy map with WMTS overlays and the “Ausschnitte” footprint layer, place combobox plus “Karten zum Stichwort …” record search and the “Karten an diesem Ort” point filter, filters + result list (owner: zurich-maps-2) |
| `detail.js` | detail panel with the IIIF viewer and the original-record link (owner: zurich-maps-3) |
| `iiif.js`, `upstream.js` | pure IIIF helpers (manifest parsing, region/zoom maths, `viewToExtent`/`extentToView` for the comparison coupling) and the one JSON-from-upstream fetch ladder — same-origin `/api/fetch` first, direct call as fallback (owner: zurich-maps-3) |
